note: GK bank item (subtopic pollution): Stockholm Convention on POPs — adopted 2001, in force 17 May 2004, eliminate/reduce POPs release. Taught in s6 from the Government of India page (Dept. of Chemicals and Petrochemicals): in force 2004 (c53), India ratified 13.01.2006 (c54), POPs definition (c52). The adoption date 22 May 2001 itself is not in the fetched gov page and is not asserted in the chapter.

Acid rain is due to increased atmospheric concentration of SO2 and NO2 (official answer D). Taught in s3 with the full chain SO2/NO2 -> sulphuric/nitric acid -> acid rain -> marble cancer (hesc118, c09); also practice q12.

Layer that prevents UV rays from reaching the earth: Stratosphere (official answer A). Taught in s4: stratosphere contains the ozone layer which absorbs UV radiation (kegy207, c45); also practice q24.

Present in a refrigerator: Chlorofluorocarbon (official answer D). Taught in s4/s2: CFCs are used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays and damage the ozone layer (hesc118, c07); also practice q22.

Noise pollution threshold: official answer 80-99 dB. The chapter teaches the Noise Rules 2000 provisions that the fetched CPCB text carries (silence zone 100 m, night loudspeaker ban, complaint at +10 dB(A)), but no fetched source states the 80 dB threshold, and the CPCB page's Schedule with zone-wise dB limits was not in the fetched text. Source gap, disclosed in the s6 exam_note box; the number is not asserted.

International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer: 16 September (official answer C). The chapter teaches the 1987 UNEP CFC-freeze agreement (jesc115, c31) but neither NCERT source gives the 16 September observance date. Source gap, disclosed in the s4 exam_note box; students are advised to memorise the date separately.

Delhi's '15-point Winter Action Plan' for air pollution: a current-affairs item tied to a specific year's government programme. Not in any textbook/government source used for this chapter and out of the chapter's textbook scope; not taught.
